name: Pathibhara Devi
tagline: Hilltop shrine at 3,794 m facing the Kanchenjunga range
meta_description: Pathibhara Devi temple guide: 3,794 m shrine in Taplejung, walking route from Kafle Pati, helicopter darshan, best months, altitude tips and yatra cost.
summary: Pathibhara Devi is a Hindu and Kirat shrine at 3,794 m above Phungling in Taplejung district. Most pilgrims drive to Kafle Pati and walk 4–5 hours up a stone stairway; helicopters land near the top in good weather. October–November and March–May are best. Sunrise over Kanchenjunga rewards an early start.
intro: Pathibhara Devi stands on a bare ridge top at 3,794 m in Taplejung district, the highest major pilgrimage site in eastern Nepal. The goddess is worshipped by Hindus as a form of Durga and by the Limbu people of the area as Mukkumlung, and pilgrims from Nepal, Sikkim, Darjeeling and Bhutan come to ask for her blessing, especially before new ventures, weddings and exams. The shrine is a small open sanctum among rocks, prayer flags and thousands of bells left by devotees whose wishes were granted.

The usual approach starts in Phungling, the Taplejung district headquarters at about 1,820 m. A rough road climbs to Kafle Pati, where the walk begins on a stone path through rhododendron and fir forest. The climb gains roughly 1,000 m in about 5 km and takes most pilgrims 4–5 hours up and 2–3 hours down. Ponies can be hired for part of the way. In clear weather the summit faces Kanchenjunga, at 8,586 m the world's third-highest mountain, about 40 km to the north.

This is real altitude. Pilgrims who fly or drive in from the plains and climb the same day often feel headache and breathlessness near the top. Walk slowly, drink water and come down if symptoms worsen. Helicopters from Phungling, Phidim, Kanyam and Dharan land near the summit in good morning weather, a popular option for older devotees. A cable car from Kafle Pati has been under construction amid local protests; check current status before you travel.
facts: Taplejung (Suketar), occasional flights; Bhadrapur for reliable flights
50 min flight to Bhadrapur + 2 days' drive, or ≈ 45 min heli shuttle from Kanyam
Wish-fulfilling goddess, bells and red cloth offerings, Kanchenjunga sunrise

highlights.title: Darshan at 3,794 m
highlights.text: The shrine is a simple open sanctum on the summit rocks, wrapped in red and gold cloth, with bells and tridents left by pilgrims. Queues build after 9 a.m. in peak months, so reaching the top by early morning gives a calmer darshan and clearer skies.

highlights.title: Sunrise over Kanchenjunga
highlights.text: On clear mornings, mostly October to December, the summit looks straight up the Tamor valley to Kanchenjunga and its satellite peaks. Pilgrims who start walking at 2 or 3 a.m. with torches arrive in time to see the first light hit the snow.

highlights.title: The stone stairway from Kafle Pati
highlights.text: The path climbs through fir, oak and rhododendron forest with tea and puja shops at intervals. It is steep but well made, and the forest is red with rhododendron in March and April. Allow 4–5 hours up at a pilgrim's pace and 2–3 hours down.

highlights.title: Helicopter darshan
highlights.text: In good weather helicopters shuttle from Phungling, Phidim, Kanyam and Dharan to a landing area near the summit. It turns a full day's climb into a morning, though weather closes flights often and the altitude still affects you on landing.

highlights.title: Limbu and Hindu traditions
highlights.text: The goddess is shared by two faiths. Limbu priests know her as Mukkumlung; Hindu pilgrims as Pathibhara Devi, a Shakti peeth for many. Animal sacrifice still takes place at a separate spot below the shrine, mostly on festival days.

highlights.title: Gateway to Kanchenjunga
highlights.text: Phungling, below the temple, is also the trailhead town for the Kanchenjunga Base Camp treks. Many trekkers add Pathibhara as an acclimatisation day trip or on the way out.

how_to_reach.text: Bhadrapur or Kakarbhitta to Ilam is ≈ 95 km and 3 hours; Ilam to Phungling via Phidim is ≈ 160 km and 7–8 hours on the Mechi Highway. From Phungling a jeep road climbs to Kafle Pati in roughly 1.5–2.5 hours depending on road condition.

From Kafle Pati the stone path gains roughly 1,000 m in about 5 km. Most pilgrims take 4–5 hours up and 2–3 down; ponies are available for part of the route in season. An older route walks up from Suketar airport in a day and a half.

Shuttle helicopters fly to a landing area near the summit from Phungling, Phidim, Kanyam and Dharan in good morning weather, taking about 5 to 30 minutes depending on the base. Charters from Bhadrapur or Biratnagar are possible; flights stop when cloud builds.

Taplejung (Suketar) airport near Phungling has had scheduled flights from Kathmandu a few days a week, about 55 minutes in a small aircraft, but seats are few and cancellations common; check current status before you travel. Bhadrapur, with several daily flights from Kathmandu, is the dependable airport for this trip.

where_to_stay: There are no hotels at the summit and overnight stays at the shrine are not the norm. Pilgrims sleep in Phungling, the Taplejung bazaar at about 1,820 m, which has a handful of simple hotels and guesthouses with hot water and dal bhat, or in basic lodges at Kafle Pati and along the lower trail that open in the pilgrim season. Expect plain rooms, shared bathrooms in the cheaper places and early starts. For more comfort, sleep in Ilam on the way up and back. We confirm named hotels with your quote.
tips: Start walking from Kafle Pati before dawn so you reach the shrine before the midday cloud and the queues.
Carry a warm jacket, gloves and a torch: the summit is often near freezing at dawn even in spring.
Drink 3 litres of water through the day and descend at once if a headache turns severe or you feel confused.
Keep small Nepali rupee notes for puja items, bells and pony fares; there is no ATM above Phungling.
Plan one spare day in Phungling for weather, especially if you are booked on a helicopter shuttle.

experiences.title: Pre-dawn climb for sunrise darshan
experiences.summary: Drive from Phungling to Kafle Pati in the dark and climb the stone path by torchlight to reach the shrine at first light, with Kanchenjunga glowing to the north, then make your offerings before the crowds and walk down through the forest.
body: This is the traditional way to visit Pathibhara. We leave Phungling around 1.30 a.m. by jeep and reach Kafle Pati in the dark. From there you climb the stone path with headtorches, stopping at tea shops that open early for pilgrims. The path gains roughly 1,000 m, so the pace is slow and steady with a short break every 20 to 30 minutes. Our guide carries a first-aid kit and a pulse oximeter.

Reaching the top by about 6 a.m. in autumn gives you the best chance of a clear sky. The Kanchenjunga massif rises up the Tamor valley to the north, and on very clear days you can pick out peaks towards Makalu in the west. After sunrise you join the queue for darshan, offer red cloth, coconut, incense and a bell if you wish, and receive tika from the priests.

The descent takes 2–3 hours and is harder on the knees than the climb, so walking poles help. We are usually back in Phungling for a late lunch. Anyone with heart or lung conditions, high blood pressure or pregnancy should talk to a doctor first and consider a pony for the climb or a helicopter.

faqs.q: How long is the walk to Pathibhara temple?
faqs.a: From Kafle Pati, the road head, the walk is about 5 km and gains roughly 1,000 m. Most pilgrims take 4–5 hours up and 2–3 hours down. Fit walkers manage it in 3 hours up. Starting from Suketar on the old trail adds most of a day.

faqs.q: Is a pony available for Pathibhara?
faqs.a: Yes, in the main seasons local handlers hire ponies for the lower and middle sections. The final steps to the shrine are walked. Fares are set locally and change each season; we arrange a pony in advance if you ask, and confirm the rate on the day.

Children aged about 8 and over who walk regularly usually manage with frequent rests. The main concern is altitude, since the shrine is at 3,794 m. Watch for headache, vomiting or unusual tiredness and turn back if they appear. For younger children a helicopter darshan is easier.

experiences.title: Helicopter shuttle darshan from Phungling
experiences.summary: Short helicopter shuttles from Phungling, Phidim or Kanyam land near the summit so you can walk the last stretch to the shrine, make your offerings and fly back the same morning, weather permitting.
body: Helicopter darshan has grown fast at Pathibhara because it removes the long climb for older and less fit pilgrims. Operators run shared shuttles in the main seasons from Phungling, Phidim, Kanyam and Dharan, filling the helicopter with four or five passengers and flying back and forth through the morning. From Phungling the flight takes only a few minutes; from Kanyam or Dharan it is closer to half an hour.

Flights only operate in clear weather, usually from first light until cloud closes in around late morning. Because of the altitude, a helicopter carries fewer people up here than on the plains, so groups may be split across two sorties. From the landing area there is still a short, steep walk to the shrine, and time on top is usually limited to around 30 to 45 minutes before the return flight. Fares are per seat, paid in Nepali rupees, and change with fuel prices.

Flying straight to 3,800 m gives your body no time to adjust. Most healthy people feel only mild breathlessness, but anyone with heart or lung disease, uncontrolled blood pressure or pregnancy should not fly to this altitude. Keep a spare day: in a cloudy week, flights may not run at all.

faqs.q: How much is the Pathibhara helicopter fare?
faqs.a: Shared seats have been quoted locally at about NPR 10,000 from Phungling, NPR 22,000 from Phidim and NPR 32,000–35,000 from Dharan or Kanyam per person, return. Prices change with fuel costs and demand, so check current status before you travel; we confirm the fare when booking.

faqs.q: Does the helicopter land at the temple?
faqs.a: It lands at a landing area near the summit, not at the shrine itself. From there you walk a short, steep section to the temple. Landing rules can change with construction and local decisions, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What happens if the helicopter cannot fly?
faqs.a: Shuttles stop when cloud covers the summit or winds are strong. You wait for the next clear morning or walk up from Kafle Pati instead. Unused seat fares are normally refunded by the operator, minus any agreed charges; we keep one spare day in every heli yatra plan.

experiences.title: Rhododendron forest walk below the shrine
experiences.summary: A gentler half-day walk on the lower forest section of the Pathibhara trail from Kafle Pati, through rhododendron, oak and fir, with tea-shop stops and views across the Tamor valley, for those who want the setting without the summit climb.
body: Not everyone in a family group wants or needs to reach the summit. This walk follows the lower part of the pilgrim path from Kafle Pati for about two hours, climbing a few hundred metres through mixed forest of rhododendron, oak and silver fir, then returns the same way. You still share the path with pilgrims, hear the bells and chants and see the puja shops that line the route.

In late March and April the rhododendron flowers red and pink across the slopes, and the forest holds birds such as laughingthrushes, minivets and sunbirds. On clear days there are views back over Phungling and down the Tamor valley. The path is stone-paved and steady, and the altitude stays below about 3,200 m, which most people manage comfortably.

This option works well as a companion trip while stronger walkers or helicopter passengers go to the top. We time it so the whole group meets again at Kafle Pati for lunch and drives back to Phungling together in the afternoon.

faqs.q: When do rhododendrons bloom at Pathibhara?
faqs.a: Usually from mid-March to late April, varying with altitude: lower slopes flower first and the higher forest follows. A cold winter can delay blooming by a week or two.

faqs.q: Is this walk suitable for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes, at a slow pace. It stays on the lower, gentler section and turns back before the steep upper stairway. Walking poles and a pony for the uphill part make it easier.

faqs.q: Do we need a guide for the forest walk?
faqs.a: The path is clear and busy in season, but a guide helps with timing, weather and coordination with the rest of your group. For foreign nationals in the wider Kanchenjunga area, licensed guides are required on trekking routes.

faqs.q: What is the height of Pathibhara Devi temple?
faqs.a: The shrine stands at 3,794 m (about 12,450 ft) on a ridge above Phungling in Taplejung district. That is higher than Muktinath at 3,710 m, so altitude sickness is possible, especially for pilgrims who come straight from the plains.

faqs.q: How do I reach Pathibhara from India?
faqs.a: Cross from Panitanki to Kakarbhitta, drive about 3 hours to Ilam, then 7–8 hours via Phidim to Phungling. Next morning drive to Kafle Pati and walk 4–5 hours to the shrine, or take a helicopter shuttle. Allow at least 5 nights from the border.

faqs.q: Pathibhara yatra package cost from India
faqs.a: Our 5-night road yatra from Bhadrapur or Kakarbhitta starts from about ₹26,000 per person, twin sharing, with private jeep, guide and simple hotels. A helicopter darshan version with 2 nights near Kanyam starts from about ₹38,000 per person. Prices depend on group size and season.

faqs.q: When is the best time for Pathibhara yatra?
faqs.a: October and November give the clearest skies and dry trails. March to May is also good, with rhododendrons in flower. December to February is cold and occasionally snowy at the top. June to September is the monsoon, with landslides on the road and leeches on the trail.

The temple stays open all year, but heavy snow can close the upper trail for days in January and February and helicopters fly less often. Winter pilgrims need warm clothing, microspikes in snowy spells and flexibility on dates.

faqs.q: Can senior citizens do Pathibhara yatra?
faqs.a: Yes, many do, using ponies or the helicopter shuttle. The main risk is altitude at 3,794 m. Seniors with heart or lung disease or high blood pressure should get medical advice first. We plan an overnight in Phungling before the climb and keep a spare day.

faqs.q: Is there a cable car to Pathibhara?
faqs.a: A 2.7 km cable car from Kafle Pati has been under construction, but it has faced court cases and local protests, and it was not operating when we last checked. Until it opens, you walk, ride a pony or fly. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Do Indian pilgrims need a permit for Pathibhara?
faqs.a: No special permit is needed for the temple. Indian citizens need a passport or voter ID to enter Nepal. Foreign nationals visiting only the temple do not need the Kanchenjunga restricted area permit, but should check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What offerings are made at Pathibhara?
faqs.a: Pilgrims usually offer red cloth, coconut, incense, flowers and sweets, and many tie a bell or offer a small trident once a wish has been granted. Animal sacrifices are made at a separate spot below the shrine, mostly on festival days. You can buy puja sets at Kafle Pati.
